sn45.134-138:2.6: chaṭṭhā navakī → chadvānavakī (sya-all) | chaṭṭhānavakī → B1 -kim.-- These parts II, III, IV of the Gaṅgāpeyyalo, -- which run on according to the pattern of I, -- are to be found in the burmese Mss. only, where they are complete with the usual abridgments, but altogether omitted in the Singhalese Mss which merely alluded to them by saying: Vārasampekhenalikhitāṁ peyyālo vitthāretabbo (S.p. 40 n 2.) -- On account of this, I suppress these texts, numbering only them and not giving more than the distinctive phrases and the reading mentions as afforded by B1-2. (pts note)
